title: Code and deploy
summary: Deploy fails, No Robot Code, RIO CPU at 100 percent, joystick unavailable, DS laptop USB.

options.label: Deploy fails, cannot find the roboRIO
Deploy works but DS says No Robot Code
Code runs but lags, loop overruns, RIO CPU near 100 percent
DS laptop USB devices keep dropping

deploy-link.question: How is the laptop connected to the roboRIO?

options.label: Ethernet or Wi-Fi through the radio

deploy-usb.title: Deploy over USB fails
steps: Open http://172.22.11.2/ in a browser.

steps.text: Does the roboRIO web page load?
steps.yes: Check the team number in WPILib Preferences.

steps: Try a different USB cable and a different laptop port. Skip hubs and extensions.
Make sure NI FRC Game Tools is installed. Without it there is no USB driver for the RIO.
Check the RIO Status light is off. A blinking Status light means the RIO is not healthy. Use the roboRIO guide.

steps.text: Are both RIO USB ports dead from static?
steps.yes: Deploy over Ethernet and swap the RIO later.

deploy-network.title: Deploy over the network fails
steps: Ping 10.TE.AM.2 from a command prompt. No reply means the network path, not the deploy. Check the RIO to radio cable and that the laptop is on the radio DS port or team Wi-Fi.
Check the team number in WPILib Preferences. Deploy looks for roboRIO-TEAM-FRC.local and 10.TE.AM.2.
Turn off Wi-Fi if using Ethernet, or unplug Ethernet if using Wi-Fi. Disable other adapters in ncpa.cpl. Two adapters confuse mDNS.
Turn off the Windows firewall. It blocks the deploy ports and mDNS.
Set the adapter to DHCP. Do not use a static 10.TE.AM.5 unless on the field.

steps.yes: Deploy over USB. Reinstall Game Tools if mDNS is broken.

crash-log.question: Open the DS Console (the gear on the right). Is there a stack trace or crash message?

crash.title: Robot code crashes at startup
steps: Read the first line of the stack trace that names a file in the team's package. That is where it died.
Check quick physical causes first. A crash is often something the code expects that is unplugged: a camera, a motor controller, or a sensor. Plug it back in and restart the code.
Check the common causes: a CAN ID that does not exist, two devices on one port or ID, a missing config file, a null used in robotInit.
Check for a vendordep version that does not match the device firmware. Update the firmware or the vendordep.
Fix, redeploy, and watch the Console again. Restart Robot Code in the DS if the RIO did not restart it.

steps.text: Does the code still crash at startup?
steps.yes: It needs deeper code work. Search the exact error text with the team.

no-code-other.title: No Robot Code with no crash shown
steps: Click Restart Robot Code in the DS and wait 20 seconds.
Do a clean build and redeploy, and let it finish fully. Teams often disconnect the laptop before the deploy completes, which leaves a corrupt deploy that will not start.
Check the WPILib year of the project matches the RIO image year. A 2025 image will not run 2024 code.
Reboot the RIO. Watch the Status light turn off, then wait for Robot Code to go green.
Open the RIO web page and confirm the team number and image version.

steps.text: Does the DS still show No Robot Code?
steps.yes: Open the DS Console and read the crash message.

cpu.title: RIO CPU at 100 percent, loop overruns, lag
steps: Open the RIO web page or the DS Diagnostics tab and read CPU. Near 100 percent starves NetworkTables and the DS packets. Comms flicker and the robot lags.
The usual cause is logging every value separately each loop. Each SmartDashboard, NetworkTables, DataLog, or Epilogue call costs time.
Disable Epilogue or DataLogManager to prove it. Then batch values into fewer entries or log at a lower rate.
Cache each CAN device read once per loop. Do not query inside the logger.
Move any vision or path planning off the RIO to a coprocessor.

steps.text: Is the RIO CPU still near 100 percent?
steps.yes: Review the periodic loop with the team.

no-motion.title: Enabled but nothing moves
steps: Check the RSL blinks and the RIO Mode light is green for teleop. A dark Mode light means the robot is not enabled.
Check the DS shows Joysticks green and the driver is on the right slot.
Watch battery voltage when enabling. A dip below 6.8 V disables outputs. Swap the battery.
Check motor controller lights. Blinking orange is valid CAN but disabled. Alternating red is no CAN. Use the CAN guide.
Read the DS Console for errors like unknown CAN ID or watchdog not fed.

steps.yes: Check CAN IDs and motor constructors with the team.

ds-usb.title: DS laptop USB devices drop
steps: Plug controllers straight into the laptop. Use a powered hub if a hub is needed. Bus powered hubs drop devices.
Remove USB extension cables. Unshielded extensions carry static that has killed ports.
Turn off USB power saving in Windows power settings and in Device Manager for each USB root hub.
Set the laptop power plan to Best Performance and never sleep.
Try a different port on the laptop.

steps.yes: Use a loaner laptop for the match.
